title: The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool Just Got a Bold New Paint Job — and Not Everyone Is Happy
summary:
Have you ever seen the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool? It’s that long, shallow pool between the Lincoln Memorial and the Washington Monument — the one where Martin Luther King Jr. gave his “I Have a Dream” speech. Well, it just got a major makeover, and it’s causing a big splash!

President Trump ordered the pool to be repainted a deep shade he calls “American flag blue.” The work was finished on Wednesday, and the pool is set to be filled with water by Sunday. Trump says the idea came from a friend visiting from Germany who thought the pool looked dark and disgusting.

But here’s the twist: Trump said the project cost between $1.5 million and $2 million. However, government records show contracts worth at least $14.8 million were awarded for the work. That’s a huge difference!

Not everyone is cheering. A group called the Cultural Landscape Foundation even filed a lawsuit to try to stop the painting, saying the dark grey-blue color makes the historic pool look like a “theme park.” A judge hasn’t ruled on the case yet, but the work is already done.

Critics also say the president is spending too much time on personal projects like this — he’s also building a big ballroom at the White House and planning a giant arch — instead of focusing on things voters care about, like the cost of living.

The pool is huge: over 2,000 feet long and originally held about 6.5 million gallons of water — that’s as much as 10 Olympic swimming pools! After a 2012 renovation, it now uses river water instead of drinking water. But with drought conditions in the area, some people wonder if refilling it is a good idea.

Love it or hate it, the Reflecting Pool is about to look very different. What do you think — cool upgrade or too much like a backyard pool?
why_it_matters: When a president changes a famous public place, it can reshape how we remember history and spark debate about what our tax dollars should pay for.

background_read: President Donald Trump (the U.S. president since 2025) ordered the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool repainted a bright blue.
The pool, on the National Mall in Washington, D.C., is where Martin Luther King Jr. delivered his famous "I Have a Dream" speech in 1963.
A historic preservation group sued, saying the dark color ruins the memorial’s serious look, while others complain the project cost much more than officials first said.
Article_Structure: WHO: President Donald Trump and the nonprofit Cultural Landscape Foundation, which sued.
WHAT: The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool was repainted a deep "American flag blue," sparking a dispute over cost ($2M vs. $14.8M) and design.
WHERE: On the National Mall in Washington, D.C., between the Lincoln Memorial and Washington Monument.
WHY: Trump believed the old pool looked dirty; critics say the change harms a historic site and wastes taxpayer money during a drought.

perspectives.description: Trump supporters say the bright blue paint makes the pool look fresh and patriotic, aligning with his vision for Washington.
Many citizens and preservationists feel the new color cheapens the memorial and that the money should have been used for drought relief or public services.
The lawsuit shows that changing national landmarks involves legal battles over historic preservation — what one leader sees as improvement, another may see as damage.
